newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF may sell 500,000 NTT shares -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF may sell 500,000 NTT shares -- paper.

text.p: The Finance Ministry may start selling 500,000 shares of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) as early as November, its fourth such sale since the telecoms giant was privatised in 1985, a local newspaper reported.
The government will start negotiations with leading underwriters on conditions of the sale in the middle of May, the Nikkan Kogyo Shimbun said in its Monday edition.
The Finance Ministry on Tuesday refused to comment on the report.
Either Daiwa Securities Co or Nikko Securities Co would be appointed lead underwriter, the paper said.
Nomura Securities Co would be avoided due to its involvement in a scandal over payments to corporate racketeers, the paper said.

The Finance Ministry currently owns 10.43 million shares, or 65.5 percent, of NTT's outstanding stock. The ministry has sold 5.5 million NTT shares since the firm's privatisation in 1985 and plans to sell another five million. The fourth tranche has been frozen since November 1988 due to weakness in the stock market.

But a recovery in NTT's share price and the government's decision to restructure NTT have prompted industry speculation that the ministry will launch a sale later this year after parliament authorises the restructuring in June or July.
"It is very likely that the Finance Ministry will finally launch the sale later this year," said Hiroyuki Iba, an analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.
NTT's shares traded around 881,000 yen in the afternoon session on Tuesday, after hovering around 800,000 yen throughout 1996.
Preferential tax treatment to be accorded to NTT and its entry into international services have been received as favourable factors for its share price, analysts said.
NTT president Junichiro Miyazu has repeatedly expressed his hope that the ministry will start selling NTT shares soon.
